questions.question: What three labels does NLI assign to a (premise, hypothesis) pair?
options: Positive / negative / neutral — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: NLI is a 3-way classification over entailment, contradiction, and neutral.

questions.question: How is NLI used as a zero-shot text classifier?
options: Verbalize each candidate label as a hypothesis (e.g. 'This text is about sports') and pick the label with the highest entailment score
By averaging embeddings, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
questions.explanation: NLI-as-classifier turns labels into hypotheses; the model picks the max-entailment label.

questions.question: Why is NLI a faithfulness check for RAG outputs?
options: It uses tokenizers, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Checking whether the retrieved context entails each answer claim is exactly the formulation NLI was trained on
questions.explanation: Hallucination = answer claims not entailed by retrieved context; NLI directly measures entailment.

questions.question: What does the hypothesis-only baseline expose?
options: Multilingual gaps, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Datasets where the hypothesis alone (without the premise) is predictive of the label, signalling label leakage
questions.explanation: A high hypothesis-only score on SNLI revealed annotation artifacts; useful for debugging your data.

questions.question: Which NLI model family tops 2026 leaderboards as the standard workhorse?
options: Plain Word2Vec — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: DeBERTa-v3 fine-tuned on MNLI and related corpora is the open NLI workhorse in 2026.

questions.question: Why do sentence-level NLI models drop accuracy on document-length premises?
options: They were trained on short premises and fail at multi-sentence and multi-hop inference; DocNLI-tuned models handle longer inputs
Documents trigger tokenizer drift, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
questions.explanation: Training distribution mismatch: single-sentence NLI models lose 20+ F1 on document-length inputs.
